summary: I fixed O-021 (M3) and O-022 (m1) in eng/rules-parity.ps1. For M3, Read-Entries now refuses any non-blank, non-comment line at column 0 after `rules:` (`^[^\s#]`), with file:line. That covers a second `rules:`, another top-level key and `---`/`...` markers. The dash checks run first, so a bare-dash entry keeps its own message. For m1, Read-Lines now refuses a lone CR, U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029 with file:line, because Python and YAML break lines there and this reader would not. C-005 gained six rows, each requiring CANNOT-READ at the right line under powershell.exe and pwsh: a second `rules:` block at the end, a `parked:` key between twinned entries, a `---` above the settled marker, and an entry hidden behind a lone CR, U+0085 or U+2028. On copies with the second-rules, parked and lone-CR shapes the committed reader said AGREE, exit 0; the fixed reader refuses all three. The regressions pass: C-001 to C-005, C-007 and the 8 rule Facts.

files.why: O-021/M3: refuses any column-0 non-comment line after `rules:`, checked after the dash checks. O-022/m1: Read-Lines refuses a lone CR, U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029 with file:line, with the characters built from [char].

O-021/O-022: six C-005 rows (second rules: block, column-0 key, --- marker, and entries hidden behind a lone CR, U+0085 and U+2028), each requiring CANNOT-READ under both shells. Get-LineOf gained a -Last switch.

obligations.how: Read-Entries now Stop-Reads on any line after `rules:` matching `^[^\s#]` that is not an entry or a bare dash. C-005 feeds a second `rules:` block appended at the end (CANNOT-READ at fitness.yaml:256), a `parked:` key before the NoBcl entry (:170) and a `---` above the settled marker (:177), each under powershell.exe and pwsh. The committed reader gave AGREE, exit 0, on the first two.

Read-Lines refuses a lone CR, U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029 with file:line and the code point. C-005 hides a whole 'Hidden (*.cs)' entry behind each of a lone CR, U+0085 and U+2028 on the NoBcl entry's `including_comments: true` line. Each gives CANNOT-READ at fitness.yaml:174 under both shells. The committed reader gave AGREE, exit 0, on the lone-CR copy.

Owed to validate-slice, and not changed this attempt. Attempt 1 ran the full harness three times with the same verdict for every row. This attempt touches only the parity reader; the C-007 clean scenario (the harness runs parity first) still passes.

follow_ups: This is the third build lap in a row sent back for the same class of finding: a YAML spelling the line reader neither reads nor refuses (M1 gaps in a list, M2 a bare dash, M3 column-0 keys, m1 odd line breaks). Each lap patched one spelling. A structural alternative is a closed grammar for everything after `rules:`: every line must be blank, a comment, `  - name:`, a key at 4 spaces, a list item at 4 or more spaces, or a scalar continuation deeper than its key, and anything else is refused. The design and the reviews asked for per-shape fixes, so that is not built here. A person should decide whether the next review lap should look for that instead of the next spelling.

Another cross-check remains available: where the TAAD engine is present, the harness already compares Fitness's loaded rule count with twinned + settled on the clean scenario, which catches any reader/YAML disagreement about the number of entries. Parity alone cannot do that without a YAML parser, which the design rules out.
